summary_paragraph: An elderly male with a history of COPD, chronic aspiration, alcohol dependence, and multiple comorbidities was readmitted from his nursing home for respiratory distress one day after discharge. He presented with hypoxia, coffee ground emesis, and leukocytosis. He was found to have an upper GI bleed, transfused one unit of blood, and remained hemodynamically stable. His respiratory status progressively worsened despite oxygen support, and he did not tolerate noninvasive ventilation. Given his DNR/DNI status and goals of care focused on comfort, antibiotics and non-essential medications were discontinued. His condition deteriorated, and he was transitioned to comfort measures only. He passed away peacefully with family notified and support provided.
problems: Pneumonitis due to inhalation of food and vomit
